name: compose/001-shop

input.text:
version: 1
project: shop
dependencies:
  kafka:
    settings:
      KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: ${endpoint}
      KAFKA_KIND: ${kind}
  payments:
    settings:
      PAYMENTS_URL: ${endpoint}
      PAYMENTS_HOST: ${host}
      PAYMENTS_PORT: ${port}
      PAYMENTS_CREDENTIALS: ${credentials}
environments:
  local:
    runtime: podman
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka

          conformance: unrated
          ports: [9092, 9644]
          config: {seed: 42}
          env: {LOG_LEVEL: debug}
      payments:
        twin:
          image: ghcr.io/example/payments-twin
          version: 2.0.0
          conformance: L1
          ports: [8080]
          endpoint: http://localhost:8080/v1
          credentials: env:PAYMENTS_TOKEN
    sync:
      - env_file: {path: .env.local}
  staging:
    runtime: aws
    cloud:
      modules: ../modules
      region: eu-west-1
      vpc_id: vpc-1
      subnet_ids: [subnet-1, subnet-2]
      cpu: 512
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka
          version: 0.1.0
          conformance: unrated
          ports: [9092]
      payments:
        real:
          endpoint: https://payments.example.com
          credentials: aws-secretsmanager:shop/payments

      - aws_appconfig: {region: eu-west-1, application: shop, profile: connections}

name: compose/005-kafka-app

input.text:
# The kafka-app's wiring: one dependency, Kafka, read through KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS, and what it
# is in each environment. The app never sees this file; it reads its setting as it always has.
version: 1
project: kafka-app

dependencies:
  kafka:
    description: The Kafka cluster the app talks to.
    settings:
      KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP_SERVERS: ${endpoint}

environments:
  # LawTwin's Kafka twin on this machine, its conformance level read from the report LawTwin
  # publishes for the release (level 3, answers), its seed fixed so a run replays byte for byte,
  # and its control plane published on 9644 for `ironframe twin kafka ...`. Build the image in the
  # lawtwin repository with `make image` until it is published.
  local:
    runtime: podman
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka
          version: 0.1.0
          conformance:
            level: answers
            report: conformance/lawtwin-kafka-0.1.0.json
          ports: [9092]
          seed: 42
          config:
            clock: frozen
          admin:
            port: 9644
    sync:
      - env_file:
          path: .env
    config_service:
      port: 8700

  # The real Kafka on this machine, run from Apache's image until the twin exists, with the
  # configuration service beside it on port 8700 (build its image with `make config-service-image`).
  local-broker:
    runtime: podman
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        real:
          endpoint: localhost:9092
          image: apache/kafka:4.1.0
          ports: [9092]
    sync:
      - env_file:
          path: .env
    config_service:
      port: 8700

  # The twin on AWS ECS Fargate, its endpoint read back from OpenTofu, and the settings synced to
  # AWS AppConfig for the app deployed beside it.
  staging:
    runtime: aws
    cloud:
      modules: ../../modules
      region: us-east-1
      vpc_id: vpc-0123456789abcdef0
      subnet_ids: [subnet-0123456789abcdef0, subnet-0fedcba9876543210]
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka
          version: 0.1.0
          conformance:
            report: conformance/lawtwin-kafka-0.1.0.json
          ports: [9092]
    sync:
      - aws_appconfig:
          region: us-east-1
          application: kafka-app
          profile: connections

  # The twin on GCP. Cloud Run serves only HTTP, so a Kafka twin, `protocol: tcp`, runs on a
  # Compute Engine instance with a reserved address it advertises to clients.
  staging-gcp:
    runtime: gcp
    cloud:
      modules: ../../modules
      project: kafka-app-staging
      region: europe-west1
      allowed_cidr_blocks: [10.0.0.0/8]
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/kafka
          version: 0.1.0
          conformance:
            report: conformance/lawtwin-kafka-0.1.0.json
          ports: [9092]
          protocol: tcp
          seed: 42
          advertise_variable: LAWTWIN_ADVERTISE
    sync:
      - gcp_parameter_manager:
          project: kafka-app-staging
          parameter: kafka-app-connections

  # The real, hosted cluster: nothing is deployed, the settings point at it.
  production:
    runtime: aws
    cloud:
      region: us-east-1
      vpc_id: vpc-0123456789abcdef0
      subnet_ids: [subnet-0123456789abcdef0]
    dependencies:
      kafka:
        real:
          endpoint: b-1.kafka-app.example.internal:9092
          credentials: aws-secretsmanager:kafka-app/production/kafka
    sync:
      - aws_appconfig:
          region: us-east-1
          application: kafka-app
          profile: connections

expected:
# Generated by ironframe from the manifest for environment local of kafka-app; edits are overwritten by `ironframe up`.
name: ironframe-kafka-app-local
services:
  ironframe-config-service:
    image: localhost/ironframe-config-service:0.1.0
    container_name: ironframe-kafka-app-local-config-service
    ports:
    - 8700:8700
    environment:
      IRONFRAME_LISTEN: 0.0.0.0:8700
      IRONFRAME_SETTINGS: /etc/ironframe/settings.json
    volumes:
    - /work/.ironframe/local/settings.json:/etc/ironframe/settings.json:ro,Z
    labels:
      io.ironframe.dependency: ironframe-config-service
      io.ironframe.environment: local
      io.ironframe.kind: config-service
      io.ironframe.project: kafka-app
  kafka:
    image: docker.io/lawtwin/kafka:0.1.0
    container_name: ironframe-kafka-app-local-kafka
    ports:
    - 9092:9092
    - 9644:9644
    environment:
      TWIN_CONFIG: '{"clock":"frozen","seed":42}'
    labels:
      io.ironframe.dependency: kafka
      io.ironframe.environment: local
      io.ironframe.kind: twin
      io.ironframe.project: kafka-app

name: compose/007-petstore-app

input.text:
# The petstore-app's wiring: one dependency, a Petstore API, read through PETSTORE_URL, and what it
# is in each environment. The app never sees this file; it reads its setting as it always has.
version: 1
project: petstore-app

dependencies:
  petstore:
    description: The Petstore API the app adds pets to.
    settings:
      PETSTORE_URL: ${endpoint}

environments:
  # LawTwin's HTTP twin serving the Petstore contract on this machine, at the level of the
  # conformance run in conformance/ (conformant), with its seed fixed, a little latency raised as
  # soon as it answers, and its control plane on 9645 so it can run beside the Kafka example's.
  # Build the image in the lawtwin repository with `make image-http` until it is published.
  local:
    runtime: podman
    dependencies:
      petstore:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/http
          version: 0.1.0
          contract: petstore
          conformance:
            level: conformant
            report: conformance/lawtwin-http-0.1.0-petstore.json
          ports: [8080]
          endpoint: http://localhost:8080
          seed: 42
          advertise_variable: LAWTWIN_ADVERTISE
          faults:
            - name: latency
              params:
                delay: 5ms
          admin:
            port: 9645
            container_port: 9644
    sync:
      - env_file:
          path: .env

  # The same twin on Cloud Run, which serves HTTP twins; its endpoint is read back from OpenTofu.
  staging:
    runtime: gcp
    cloud:
      modules: ../../modules
      project: petstore-app-staging
      region: europe-west1
    dependencies:
      petstore:
        twin:
          image: lawtwin/http
          version: 0.1.0
          contract: petstore
          conformance:
            report: conformance/lawtwin-http-0.1.0-petstore.json
          ports: [8080]
          seed: 42
    sync:
      - gcp_parameter_manager:
          project: petstore-app-staging
          parameter: petstore-app-connections

expected:
# Generated by ironframe from the manifest for environment local of petstore-app; edits are overwritten by `ironframe up`.
name: ironframe-petstore-app-local
services:
  petstore:
    image: docker.io/lawtwin/http:0.1.0
    container_name: ironframe-petstore-app-local-petstore
    ports:
    - 8080:8080
    - 9645:9644
    environment:
      LAWTWIN_ADVERTISE: localhost:8080
      TWIN_CONFIG: '{"seed":42,"contract":"petstore"}'
    labels:
      io.ironframe.dependency: petstore
      io.ironframe.environment: local
      io.ironframe.kind: twin
      io.ironframe.project: petstore-app
